Name: adjacent
Summary: Evaluates an operation against every consecutive pair of input values. Returns `null` when the input cannot be evaluated.

Parameters.Name: operation
Parameters.Summary: Specifies the callable or open expression evaluated against each consecutive pair.

Behavior:
`adjacent` evaluates the supplied operation against each consecutive pair of values.

For each pair, the first value becomes the input of the operation and the second value is supplied as its missing argument. This means that a binary function such as `subtract` can be passed directly.

For example, `{1, 2, 3} | adjacent(subtract)` is conceptually equivalent to applying `$1 | subtract($0)` to each consecutive pair.

Name: array
Summary: Constructs a new array by evaluating zero or more positional expressions from left to right against the same input. Spread arguments expand array values in place. This is the runtime-expression counterpart of array literal syntax.

Parameters.Name: values
Parameters.Summary: Zero or more expressions whose evaluated values become the elements of the resulting array.

Name: broadcast
Summary: Executes an accumulator once over the full input enumerable, then returns the final accumulated value repeated once for each input element. Returns `null` when the input is not an enumerable or is a string.

Parameters.Name: accumulator
Parameters.Summary: Factory that creates the accumulator instance used for the broadcast execution.

Name: chunk
Summary: Splits an array into consecutive, non-overlapping chunks of at most the specified size, preserving a final partial chunk. It resembles a count-based tumbling window but, unlike general sliding or hopping windows, has no separate step and always keeps the final partial chunk. It does not group items by inactivity or time. Returns `null` when the input cannot be evaluated.

Parameters.Name: size
Parameters.Summary: The strictly positive number of items in each chunk.

Name: filter
Summary: Applies a predicate expression to each input item and returns only items for which the predicate evaluates to `true`. Returns `null` when the input is not an enumerable or is a string.

Parameters.Name: predicate
Parameters.Summary: Expression defining the predicate applied to each input item.

Name: first-elements
Summary: Returns up to the requested number of elements from the start of the input enumerable. Returns `null` when the input is not an enumerable, is a string, or the count is negative.

Parameters.Name: count
Parameters.Summary: Number of elements to return from the start of the input.

Name: fold
Summary: Executes an accumulator once over the full input enumerable and returns the final accumulated value. Returns `null` when the input is not an enumerable or is a string.

Parameters.Name: accumulator
Parameters.Summary: Factory that creates the accumulator instance used for the fold execution.

Name: lag
Summary: Returns the previous value for each input element. The first output value is `null` because there is no previous element. Preserves input cardinality (one output item per input item). Returns `null` when the input is not an enumerable or is a string.

Name: last-elements
Summary: Returns up to the requested number of elements from the end of the input enumerable, preserving their order. Returns `null` when the input is not an enumerable, is a string, or the count is negative.

Parameters.Name: count
Parameters.Summary: Number of elements to return from the end of the input.

Name: lead
Summary: Returns the next value for each input element. The last output value is `null` because there is no next element. Preserves input cardinality (one output item per input item). Returns `null` when the input is not an enumerable or is a string.

Name: map
Summary: Applies a transformation expression to each input item and returns the transformed values. Preserves input cardinality (one output item per input item). Returns `null` when the input is not an enumerable or is a string.

Parameters.Name: transformation
Parameters.Summary: Expression creating the transformation applied to each input item.

Name: pairwise
Summary: Returns each consecutive pair of input values as a tuple. Returns `null` when the input cannot be evaluated.

Name: reverse
Summary: Returns the input enumerable with elements emitted in the opposite order. Preserves input cardinality (one output item per input item). Returns `null` when the input is not an enumerable or is a string.

Name: scan
Summary: Executes an accumulator progressively over the input enumerable and returns the intermediate accumulated value after each input element. Preserves input cardinality (one output item per input item). This differs from fold (final value only) and broadcast (final value repeated). Returns `null` when the input is not an enumerable or is a string.

Parameters.Name: accumulator
Parameters.Summary: Factory that creates the accumulator instance used for the scan execution.

Name: skip-first-elements
Summary: Omits the requested number of elements from the start of the input enumerable and returns the remainder. Returns `null` when the input is not an enumerable, is a string, or the count is negative.

Parameters.Name: count
Parameters.Summary: Number of elements to omit from the start of the input.

Name: skip-last-elements
Summary: Omits the requested number of elements from the end of the input enumerable and returns the remainder. Returns `null` when the input is not an enumerable, is a string, or the count is negative.

Parameters.Name: count
Parameters.Summary: Number of elements to omit from the end of the input.

Name: slice-elements
Summary: Returns the elements in the zero-based half-open range from start, inclusive, to end, exclusive. Returns `null` when the input is not an enumerable, is a string, or either bound is negative.

Parameters.Name: start
Parameters.Summary: Zero-based index of the first element to return.

Parameters.Name: end
Parameters.Summary: Zero-based exclusive index at which to stop returning elements.

Name: complement
Summary: Returns the distinct values from the specified array that do not appear in the pipeline input, preserving the specified array order. Returns `null` when the input cannot be evaluated.

Parameters.Name: array
Parameters.Summary: Specifies the reference array from which values present in the pipeline input are excluded.

Name: difference
Summary: Returns the distinct values from the pipeline input that do not appear in the specified array, preserving the pipeline input order. Returns `null` when the input cannot be evaluated.

Parameters.Name: array
Parameters.Summary: Specifies the array containing values to exclude from the pipeline input.

Name: distinct
Summary: Returns the unique values from the input array in the order of their first occurrence. Returns `null` when the input cannot be evaluated.

Name: intersection
Summary: Returns the distinct values found in both the pipeline input and the specified array, preserving the pipeline input order. Returns `null` when the input cannot be evaluated.

Parameters.Name: array
Parameters.Summary: Specifies the array to compare with the pipeline input.

Name: symmetric-difference
Summary: Returns the distinct values that appear in exactly one of the two arrays, listing pipeline-input exclusives first and parameter-array exclusives second while preserving order within each source. Returns `null` when the input cannot be evaluated.

Parameters.Name: array
Parameters.Summary: Specifies the second array to compare against the pipeline input.

Name: union
Summary: Returns the distinct values appearing in either the pipeline input or the specified array, listing pipeline-input values first and argument-only values second while preserving order within each source. Returns `null` when the input cannot be evaluated.

Parameters.Name: array
Parameters.Summary: Specifies the second array whose values are combined with the pipeline input.

Name: creation-datetime
Summary: Returns the creation time of the file provided as argument in local time.

Name: creation-datetime-utc
Summary: Returns the creation time of the file provided as argument in UTC.

Name: directory
Summary: Returns the directory information of a file path provided as argument. The value is always ending by `/` character. Returns `empty` if path does not contain root directory information or is `null`.

Name: extension
Summary: Returns the extension of a file path provided as argument.

Name: filename
Summary: Returns the file name and extension of a file path provided as argument.

Name: filename-without-extension
Summary: Returns the file name without the extension of a file path provided as argument.

Name: root
Summary: Returns the root directory information of a file path provided as argument. Returns `empty` if path does not contain root directory information or is `null`.

Name: size
Summary: Returns the size of the file provided as argument in bytes.

Name: update-datetime
Summary: Returns the last update time of the file provided as argument in local time.

Name: update-datetime-utc
Summary: Returns the last update time of the file provided as argument in UTC.

Name: absolute
Summary: Returns the absolute value of the argument value.

Name: add
Summary: Returns the sum of the input value and the parameter value.

Parameters.Name: value
Parameters.Summary: The value to add to the input value.

Parameters.Name: times
Parameters.Summary: Number of times the addition is applied.

Name: cube-power
Summary: Returns the the numeric argument value raised to the cube power.

Name: cube-root
Summary: Returns cube root of the numeric argument value.

Name: decrement
Summary: Returns the argument number decremented of one unit.

Name: divide
Summary: Returns the argument number divided by the parameter value. If the parameter value is `0`, it returns `null`.

Parameters.Name: value
Parameters.Summary: The value to divide the argument value.

Name: greatest-common-divisor
Summary: Returns the greatest common divisor (GCD) of the argument integer and the parameter integer. Returns `null` if the argument is not an integer.

Parameters.Name: value
Parameters.Summary: The integer used to compute the greatest common divisor with the argument value.

Name: increment
Summary: Returns the argument number incremented of one unit.

Name: invert
Summary: Returns the reciprocal of the argument number, meaning the result of the division of 1 by the argument number. If the argument value is `0`, it returns `null`.

Name: lowest-common-multiple
Summary: Returns the lowest common multiple (LCM) of the argument integer and the parameter integer. Returns `null` if the argument is not an integer.

Parameters.Name: value
Parameters.Summary: The integer used to compute the lowest common multiple with the argument value.

Name: multiply
Summary: Returns the argument number multiplied by the parameter value.

Parameters.Name: value
Parameters.Summary: The value to be multiplied by the argument value.

Name: nth-root
Summary: Returns the root specified by the parameter value of the numeric argument value.

Name: oppose
Summary: Returns the integer being the additive inverse of the argument meaning that their sum is equal to zero. The opposite of 0 is 0.

Name: percent-change
Summary: Returns the percentage change from the previous numeric value to the current input value. Returns `null` when the input or parameter cannot be evaluated or when the previous value is zero.

Parameters.Name: previous
Parameters.Summary: Specifies the previous numeric value used as the percentage-change baseline.

Name: power
Summary: Returns the the numeric argument value raised to the power specified by the parameter value.

Name: sign
Summary: Returns an integer that indicates the sign of the argument value. It returns -1 if the value is strictly negative, 0 if the value is 0 and 1 if the value is strictly positive.

Name: square-power
Summary: Returns the the numeric argument value raised to the square power.

Name: square-root
Summary: Returns square root of the numeric argument value.

Name: subtract
Summary: Returns the difference between the argument number and the parameter value.

Parameters.Name: value
Parameters.Summary: The value to be subtracted to the argument value.

Parameters.Name: times
Parameters.Summary: An integer between 0 and +Infinity, indicating the number of times to repeat the subtraction.

Name: null-to-zero
Summary: Returns the unmodified argument value except if the argument value is `null`, `empty` or `whitespace` then it returns `0`.

Name: human-readable-format-binary-bytes
Summary: Formats a numeric value as binary bytes using IEC prefixes.

Name: human-readable-format-decimal
Summary: Formats a numeric value using decimal SI prefixes.

Name: human-readable-format-decimal-bytes
Summary: Formats a numeric value as decimal bytes using SI prefixes.

Name: ceiling
Summary: Returns the smallest integer greater than or equal to the argument number.

Name: clip
Summary: Returns the value of an argument number, unless it is smaller than min, in which case it returns min, or greater than max, in which case it returns max.

Parameters.Name: min
Parameters.Summary: value returned in case the argument value is smaller than it.

Parameters.Name: max
Parameters.Summary: value returned in case the argument value is greater than it.

Name: floor
Summary: Returns the largest integer less than or equal to the argument number.

Name: integer
Summary: Returns the value of an argument number rounded to the nearest integer.

Name: round
Summary: Returns the value of an argument number to the specified number of fractional digits.

Parameters.Name: digits
Parameters.Summary: An integer between 0 and +Infinity, indicating the number of fractional digits in the return value.

Name: field
Summary: Returns the value of the named field from the input record or object. Returns `null` when the field does not exist or the input does not expose named values.

Parameters.Name: name
Parameters.Summary: Name of the field to retrieve from the input.

Name: record
Summary: Creates a record by evaluating its named and spread entries against the input value. Later entries overwrite fields with the same name created by earlier entries.

Parameters.Name: entries
Parameters.Summary: Zero or more named or spread entries used to construct the resulting record. Each entry is evaluated against the input value.

Name: any-to-any
Summary: Returns `any`.

Name: coalesce
Summary: Returns the first non-null result from two or more expressions evaluated from left to right against the same input. Returns `null` when every expression evaluates to `null`.

Parameters.Name: expressions
Parameters.Summary: Two or more candidate expressions evaluated from left to right against the same input.

Name: coerce-boolean
Summary: Attempts to convert the input to a boolean value. Returns `null` when the input cannot be converted.

Name: coerce-date
Summary: Attempts to convert the input to a date value. Returns `null` when the input cannot be converted.

Name: coerce-datetime
Summary: Attempts to convert the input to a date-time value. Returns `null` when the input cannot be converted.

Name: coerce-int
Summary: Attempts to convert the input to an integer value. Returns `null` when the input cannot be converted without loss.

Name: coerce-numeric
Summary: Attempts to convert the input to a numeric value. Returns `null` when the input cannot be converted.

Name: coerce-text
Input: boolean | date | date-time | integer | numeric | text | year-month
Summary: Attempts to convert the input to a text value. Returns `null` when the input cannot be converted.

Name: coerce-time
Summary: Attempts to convert the input to a time value. Returns `null` when the input cannot be converted.

Name: neutral
Summary: Returns the argument value.

Name: null-to-value
Summary: Returns the value passed as argument, except if the value is `null` then it returns `value`.

Name: arity
Summary: Returns the number of positional elements in the input tuple.

Name: swap
Summary: Returns a tuple with two positions exchanged, defaulting to the first and last positions.

Parameters.Name: first
Parameters.Summary: Specifies the first zero-based position.

Parameters.Name: second
Parameters.Summary: Specifies the second zero-based position.

Name: extend
Summary: Returns a new tuple with a value appended, expanding tuple values into their positions.

Parameters.Name: value
Parameters.Summary: Specifies the value to append; tuple values are expanded into their positions.

Name: pick
Summary: Returns a tuple containing selected positions in the requested order.

Parameters.Name: positions
Parameters.Summary: One or more zero-based tuple positions.

Name: apply
Summary: Evaluates an expression with the input tuple as its positional context.

Parameters.Name: expression
Parameters.Summary: Specifies the expression evaluated against the tuple.

Name: tuple-at
Summary: Returns the tuple field at the specified zero-based position. Returns `null` when the input is not a tuple or the position is out of range.

Parameters.Name: position
Parameters.Summary: Specifies the zero-based position of the tuple field to return.

Name: tuple-first
Summary: Returns the first field of a tuple. Returns `null` when the input is not a tuple.

Name: tuple-second
Summary: Returns the second field of a tuple. Returns `null` when the input is not a tuple.

Name: value-to-value
Summary: Returns `value` except if the argument value is `null` then it returns `null`.

Name: age
Summary: Returns how many years separate the argument dateTime and now.

Name: backward
Summary: Returns a dateTime that subtract the timestamp passed as parameter to the argument. If times is specified this operation is reproduced.

Parameters.Name: time
Parameters.Summary: The value to be subtracted to the argument value.

Parameters.Name: times
Parameters.Summary: An integer between 0 and +Infinity, indicating the number of times to repeat the subtraction

Name: ceiling-hour
Summary: Returns the dateTime passed as argument value with the minutes, seconds and milliseconds set to zero and an hour added.

Name: ceiling-minute
Summary: Returns the dateTime passed as argument value with the seconds and milliseconds set to zero and a minute added.

Name: change-of-hour
Summary: returns a temporal value corresponding to the same instant of the argument value but with a new value for the second part.

Name: change-of-minute
Summary: returns a temporal value corresponding to the same instant of the argument value but with a new value for the second part.

Name: change-of-month
Summary: returns a temporal value corresponding to the same day and year of the argument value but of the month passed as the parameter. If the original day is 29, 30, or 31 and the new month passed as a parameter has fewer days then it returns the last day of the corresponding month.

Name: change-of-second
Summary: returns a temporal value corresponding to the same instant of the argument value but with a new value for the second part.

Name: change-of-year
Summary: returns a temporal value corresponding to the same day and month of the argument value but of the year passed as the parameter. If the original date was the 29th of February and the year passed as a parameter is not a leap year then it returns the 28th of February.

Name: clamp
Summary: Returns the value of an argument dateTime, unless it is before min (in which case it returns min), or after max (in which case it returns max).

Parameters.Name: min
Parameters.Summary: value returned in case the argument value is before than it

Parameters.Name: max
Parameters.Summary: value returned in case the argument value is after than it

Name: day-of-month
Summary: returns a numeric value representing the day of the month of the date passed as the argument

Name: day-of-week
Summary: returns a numeric value representing the day of the week (1 being Monday and 7 being Sunday) of the date passed as the argument

Name: day-of-year
Summary: returns a numeric value representing the day position within the year of the date passed as the argument

Name: duration-between
Summary: Returns the signed duration between the current temporal value and a previous temporal value. Returns `null` when either value cannot be evaluated or the temporal values are incompatible.

Parameters.Name: previous
Parameters.Summary: The previous temporal value to subtract from the current input.

Name: floor-hour
Summary: Returns the dateTime passed as argument value with the minutes, seconds and milliseconds set to zero.

Name: floor-minute
Summary: Returns the dateTime passed as argument value with the seconds and milliseconds set to zero.

Name: forward
Summary: Returns a dateTime that adds the timestamp passed as parameter to the argument. If times is specified this operation is reproduced.

Parameters.Name: time
Parameters.Summary: The value to be added to the argument value

Parameters.Name: times
Parameters.Summary: An integer between 0 and +Infinity, indicating the number of times to repeat the addition

Name: hour
Summary: returns a textual value at format hh (24 hours format) representing the hours of the dateTime passed as the argument

Name: hour-minute
Summary: returns a textual value at format hh:mm (24 hours format) representing the hours and minutes of the dateTime passed as the argument

Name: hour-minute-second
Summary: returns a textual value at format hh:mm:ss (24 hours format) representing the hours, minutes, and seconds of the dateTime passed as the argument

Name: hour-of-day
Summary: returns a numeric value representing the hours of the date passed as the argument

Name: iso-day-of-year
Summary: returns a numeric value representing the day position within the year of the date passed as the argument

Name: iso-week-of-year
Summary: returns a textual value at format YYYY-Www representing the year and week number (according to ISO 8601) of the date passed as the argument

Name: iso-year-day
Summary: returns a textual value at format YYYY-ddd representing the year, and the day number of the date passed as the argument (both according to ISO 8601)

Name: iso-year-week
Summary: returns a textual value at format YYYY-Www representing the year and week number (according to ISO 8601) of the date passed as the argument

Name: iso-year-week-day
Summary: returns a textual value at format YYYY-Www-D representing the year and week number (according to ISO 8601), and the day number (1 being Monday) of the date passed as the argument

Name: local-to-utc
Summary: Returns the dateTime passed as argument and set in the time zone passed as parameter converted to UTC.

Name: minute-of-day
Summary: returns a numeric value representing the minutes of the date passed as the argument

Name: minute-of-hour
Summary: returns a numeric value representing the minutes of the hour passed as the argument

Name: month
Summary: returns a textual value at format MM representing the month of the date passed as the argument

Name: month-day
Summary: returns a textual value at format MM-DD representing the month and day of the date passed as the argument

Name: month-of-year
Summary: returns a numeric value representing the month of the date passed as the argument

Name: next-business-days
Summary: Returns a new date value corresponding to the date passed as the argument, counting forward the business days (being weekdays different of Saturday and Sunday) specified as the parameter. It always returns a business day, as such if the date passed as the argument is a weekend, it considers that this date was the Friday before the argument value.

Parameters.Name: count
Parameters.Summary: The count of business days to move forward.

Name: next-day
Summary: Returns the day immediately following the dateTime passed as argument value.

Name: next-month
Summary: Returns the dateTime that adds a month to the dateTime passed as argument value.

Name: next-weekday
Summary: Returns a new date value corresponding to the occurrence of the weekday, passed as a parameter, following the date passed as the argument.

Parameters.Name: weekday
Parameters.Summary: The day of week to compare to the argument.

Name: next-weekday-or-same
Summary: Returns a new date value corresponding to the occurrence of the weekday passed as a parameter following the date passed as the argument except if this date corresponds to the expected weekday then it returns this date.

Parameters.Name: weekday
Parameters.Summary: The day of week to compare to the argument.

Name: next-year
Summary: Returns the dateTime that adds a year to the dateTime passed as argument value.

Name: previous-business-days
Summary: Returns a new date value corresponding to the date passed as the argument, counting backward the business days (being weekdays different of Saturday and Sunday) specified as the parameter. It always returns a business day, as such if the date passed as the argument is a weekend, it considers that this date was the Friday before the argument value.

Parameters.Name: count
Parameters.Summary: The count of business days to move forward.

Name: previous-day
Summary: Returns the dateTime that substract a day to the dateTime passed as argument value.

Name: previous-month
Summary: Returns the dateTime that substract a month to the dateTime passed as argument value.

Name: previous-weekday
Summary: Returns a new date value corresponding to the occurrence of the weekday passed as a parameter preceding the date passed as the argument.

Parameters.Name: weekday
Parameters.Summary: The day of week to compare to the argument.

Name: previous-weekday-or-same
Summary: Returns a new date value corresponding to the occurrence of the weekday passed as a parameter preceding the date passed as the argument except if this date corresponds to the expected weekday then it returns this date.

Parameters.Name: weekday
Parameters.Summary: The day of week to compare to the argument.

Name: previous-year
Summary: Returns the dateTime that substract a year to the dateTime passed as argument value.

Name: second-of-day
Summary: returns a numeric value representing the seconds of the day of the date passed as the argument

Name: second-of-hour
Summary: returns a numeric value representing the seconds of the hour of the date passed as the argument

Name: second-of-minute
Summary: returns a numeric value representing the seconds of the minute of the date passed as the argument

Name: set-time
Summary: Returns a dateTime with the time part set to the value passed as parameter and the date part corresponding to the argument value.

Parameters.Name: instant
Parameters.Summary: The time value to set as hours, minutes, seconds of the dateTime argument

Name: set-to-local
Summary: Returns the dateTime passed as argument without changing the current hours/minutes and sets the kind to local

Name: set-to-utc
Summary: Returns the dateTime passed as argument without changing the current hours/minutes and sets the kind to UTC

Name: utc-to-local
Summary: Returns the dateTime passed as argument and set in UTC converted to the time zone passed as parameter.

Name: year
Summary: returns a textual value at format YYYY representing the year of the date passed as the argument

Name: year-of-era
Summary: returns a numeric value representing the year of the date passed as the argument

Name: catholic-calendar
Summary: Returns the date of the Catholic calendar event passed as parameter for the year specified by the argument. Returns `null` if the event is unknown.

Name: first-in-month
Summary: Returns a new date value corresponding to the first occurrence of the weekday passed as a parameter of the month of the date passed as the argument.

Parameters.Name: weekday
Parameters.Summary: The day of week to compare to the argument.

Name: first-of-month
Summary: Returns the first day of the month of the same month/year than the argument dateTime.

Name: first-of-year
Summary: Returns the first of January of the same year than the argument dateTime.

Name: last-in-month
Summary: Returns a new dateTime value corresponding to the last occurrence of the weekday passed as a parameter of the month of the date passed as the argument.

Parameters.Name: weekday
Parameters.Summary: The day of week to compare to the argument.

Name: last-of-month
Summary: Returns the last day of the month of the same month/year than the argument dateTime.

Name: last-of-year
Summary: Returns the 31st of December of the same year than the argument dateTime.

Name: length-of-month
Summary: returns the count of days within the month of the dateTime value passed as the argument. If the argument is not a dateTime but a text at format "YYYY-MM", it returns count of days of the month represented by this value. It returns a value between 28 and 31 (depending of leap year and month).

Name: length-of-year
Summary: Returns the count of days within the year of the dateTime value passed as the argument. If the argument is not a dateTime but an integer, returns count of days of the corresponding year. It returns 365 or 366 (for leap years).

Name: datetime-to-date
Summary: Returns the date at midnight of the argument dateTime.

Name: invalid-to-date
Summary: Returns the dateTime argument except if the value is not a valid dateTime then it returns the parameter value.

Parameters.Name: default
Parameters.Summary: The dateTime to be returned if the argument is not a valid dateTime.

Name: null-to-date
Summary: Returns the dateTime argument except if the value is `null` then it returns the parameter value.

Parameters.Name: default
Parameters.Summary: The dateTime to be returned if the argument is `null`.

Name: after-substring
Summary: Returns the substring of the argument string, containing all the characters immediately following the first occurrence of the string passed in parameter. If the parameter value is `null` or `empty` then the argument value is returned.

Parameters.Name: substring
Parameters.Summary: The string to seek.

Parameters.Name: count
Parameters.Summary: The number of character positions to examine.

Name: allcaps-case
Summary: Returns the input text in ALLCAPS case, uppercasing words and concatenating them without separators. Returns empty text when the input is `null`, `empty`, `blank`, or a zero-length array.

Name: append
Summary: Returns the argument value followed by the parameter value. If the argument is `null`, it returns the text specified as the parameter.

Parameters.Name: text
Parameters.Summary: The text to append

Name: append-new-line
Summary: Returns the argument value followed by a space character. If the argument is `null`, it returns the text specified as the parameter.

Name: append-space
Summary: Returns the argument value followed by a space character. If the argument is `null`, it returns the text specified as the parameter.

Name: before-substring
Summary: Returns the substring of the argument string, containing all the characters immediately preceding the first occurrence of the string passed in parameter. If the parameter value is `null` or `empty` then the function returns `empty`.

Parameters.Name: substring
Parameters.Summary: The string to seek.

Parameters.Name: count
Parameters.Summary: The number of character positions to examine.

Name: camel-case
Summary: Returns the input text in camelCase, lowercasing the first word and capitalizing subsequent words without separators. Returns empty text when the input is `null`, `empty`, `blank`, or a zero-length array.

Name: camel-snake-case
Summary: Returns the input text in camel_Snake case, lowercasing the first word, capitalizing subsequent words, and joining them with underscores. Returns empty text when the input is `null`, `empty`, `blank`, or a zero-length array.

Name: cobol-case
Summary: Returns the input text in COBOL-CASE, uppercasing words and joining them with hyphens. Returns empty text when the input is `null`, `empty`, `blank`, or a zero-length array.

Name: count-distinct-chars
Summary: Returns the count of distinct chars in the textual argument value. If the value is `null` or `empty` then it returns `0`. If the value is `blank` then it returns `-1`.

Name: count-substring
Summary: Returns the count of non-overlapping occurrences of a substring, defined as a parameter, in the argument value.

Parameters.Name: substring
Parameters.Summary: The substring to count in the argument value.

Name: dot-case
Summary: Returns the input text in dot.case, lowercasing words and joining them with periods. Returns empty text when the input is `null`, `empty`, `blank`, or a zero-length array.

Name: empty-to-null
Summary: Returns the argument value except if this value is `empty` then it returns `null`.

Name: filter-chars
Summary: Returns only those characters specified in the parameter, in the order, they were originally entered in the input value.

Parameters.Name: filter
Parameters.Summary: The chars to filter from the argument string.

Name: first-chars
Summary: Returns the first chars of the argument value. The length of the string returned is maximum the parameter value, if the argument string is smaller then the full string is returned.

Parameters.Name: length
Parameters.Summary: An integer value between 0 and +Infinity, defining the length of the substring to return.

Name: flat-case
Summary: Returns the input text in flatcase, lowercasing words and concatenating them without separators. Returns empty text when the input is `null`, `empty`, `blank`, or a zero-length array.

Name: html-to-text
Summary: Returns the argument value that has previously been HTML-encoded into a decoded string.

Name: kebab-case
Summary: Returns the input text in kebab-case, lowercasing words and joining them with hyphens. Returns empty text when the input is `null`, `empty`, `blank`, or a zero-length array.

Name: last-chars
Summary: Returns the last chars of the argument value. The length of the string returned is maximum the parameter value, if the argument string is smaller then the full string is returned.

Parameters.Name: length
Parameters.Summary: An integer value between 0 and +Infinity, defining the length of the substring to return.

Name: length
Summary: Returns the length of the argument value. If the value is `null` or `empty` then it returns `0`. If the value is `blank` then it returns `-1`.

Name: lower
Summary: Returns the input text converted to lowercase using invariant culture rules. Returns `null` when the input is `null`, `DBNull`, `(null)`, or a zero-length array.

Name: mask-to-text
Summary: Returns the value that passed to the function TextToMask will return the argument value. If the length of the mask and the length of the argument value are not equal the function returns `null`. If the non-asterisk characters are not matching between the mask and the argument value then the function also returns `null`.

Parameters.Name: mask
Parameters.Summary: The string representing the mask to be unset from the argument string.

Name: namespace-case
Summary: Returns the input text in namespace::case, lowercasing words and joining them with double colons. Returns empty text when the input is `null`, `empty`, `blank`, or a zero-length array.

Name: null-to-empty
Summary: Returns the argument value except if this value is `null` then it returns `empty`.

Name: pad-center
Summary: Returns a new string that center-aligns the characters in this string by padding them on both the left and the right with a specified character, for a specified total length. If the padding cannot be symetrical then the padding char is added on the right. If the length of the argument value is longer than the parameter value then the argument value is returned unmodified.

Parameters.Name: length
Parameters.Summary: An integer value between 0 and +Infinity, defining the minimal length of the string returned

Parameters.Name: character
Parameters.Summary: The padding character

Name: pad-left
Summary: Returns a new string that right-aligns the characters in this string by padding them on the left with a specified character, for a specified total length. If the length of the argument value is longer than the parameter value then the argument value is returned unmodified.

Parameters.Name: length
Parameters.Summary: An integer value between 0 and +Infinity, defining the minimal length of the string returned

Parameters.Name: character
Parameters.Summary: The padding character

Name: pad-right
Summary: Returns a new string that left-aligns the characters in this string by padding them on the right with a specified character, for a specified total length. If the length of the argument value is longer than the parameter value then the argument value is returned unmodified.

Parameters.Name: length
Parameters.Summary: An integer value between 0 and +Infinity, defining the minimal length of the string returned

Parameters.Name: character
Parameters.Summary: The padding character

Name: pascal-case
Summary: Returns the input text in PascalCase, capitalizing each word and removing separators. Returns empty text when the input is `null`, `empty`, `blank`, or a zero-length array.

Name: pascal-snake-case
Summary: Returns the input text in Pascal_Snake case, capitalizing each word and joining them with underscores. Returns empty text when the input is `null`, `empty`, `blank`, or a zero-length array.

Name: path-case
Summary: Returns the input text in path/case, lowercasing words and joining them with slashes. Returns empty text when the input is `null`, `empty`, `blank`, or a zero-length array.

Name: prefix
Summary: Returns the argument value preceeded by the parameter value. If the argument is `null`, it returns `null`.

Parameters.Name: prefix
Parameters.Summary: The text to append

Name: prefix-new-line
Summary: Returns the argument value preceeded by a space character. If the argument is `null`, it returns `null`.

Name: prefix-space
Summary: Returns the argument value preceeded by a space character. If the argument is `null`, it returns `null`.

Name: prepend
Summary: Returns the argument value preceeded by the parameter value. If the argument is `null`, it returns the text specified as the parameter.

Parameters.Name: text
Parameters.Summary: The text to prepend

Name: prepend-new-line
Summary: Returns the argument value preceeded by a space character. If the argument is `null`, it returns the text specified as the parameter.

Name: prepend-space
Summary: Returns the argument value preceeded by a space character. If the argument is `null`, it returns the text specified as the parameter.

Name: remove-chars
Summary: Returns the argument value without the specified character. If the argument and the parameter values are white-space characters then it returns `empty`.

Parameters.Name: charToRemove
Parameters.Summary: The char to be removed from the argument string.

Name: replace-chars
Summary: Returns the argument value where a specific char has been replaced by another, both specified as parameters.

Parameters.Name: charToReplace
Parameters.Summary: The char to be replaced from the argument string.

Parameters.Name: charReplacing
Parameters.Summary: The replacing char from the argument string.

Name: replace-slice
Summary: Returns the argument value with a subset of the string substitued by a another string.

Parameters.Name: start
Parameters.Summary: The position to start to replace

Parameters.Name: length
Parameters.Summary: The length to replace

Parameters.Name: append
Parameters.Summary: The text to append when the slice has been removed

Name: retain-alpha
Summary: Returns the input string with all characters removed except for letters (A-Z, a-z). If the argument is `null`, it returns `null`.

Name: retain-alpha-numeric
Summary: Returns the input string with all characters removed except for letters (A-Z, a-z) and digits (0-9). If the argument is `null`, it returns `null`.

Name: retain-numeric
Summary: Returns the input string with all non-numeric characters removed, leaving only digits (0-9).. If the argument is `null`, it returns `null`.

Name: retain-numeric-symbol
Summary: Returns the input string with all characters removed except for digits (0-9) and the symbols `+`, `-`, `,` and `.` If the argument is `null`, it returns `null`.

Name: screaming-snake-case
Summary: Returns the input text in SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE, uppercasing words and joining them with underscores. Returns empty text when the input is `null`, `empty`, `blank`, or a zero-length array.

Name: sentence-case
Summary: Returns the input text in sentence case by capitalizing the first word while preserving the remaining content. Words containing dots, ampersands, or uppercase letters beyond the first character are treated as already correctly cased and preserved as-is (for example `example.com`, `AT&T`, and `iTunes`). Returns `null` when the input is `null`, `DBNull`, `(null)`, or a zero-length array.

Name: skip-first-chars
Summary: Returns the last chars of the argument value. The length of the string omitted at the beginning of the argument value is equal to the parameter value. If the length of the argument value is smaller or equal to the parameter value then the functions returns `empty`.

Parameters.Name: length
Parameters.Summary: An integer value between 0 and +Infinity, defining the length of the substring to skip.

Name: skip-last-chars
Summary: Returns the first chars of the argument value. The length of the string omitted at the end of the argument value is equal to the parameter value. If the length of the argument value is smaller or equal to the parameter value then the functions returns `empty`.

Parameters.Name: length
Parameters.Summary: An integer value between 0 and +Infinity, defining the length of the substring to skip.

Name: snake-case
Summary: Returns the input text in snake_case, lowercasing words and joining them with underscores. Returns empty text when the input is `null`, `empty`, `blank`, or a zero-length array.

Name: suffix
Summary: Returns the argument value followed by the parameter value. If the argument is `null`, it returns `null`.

Parameters.Name: suffix
Parameters.Summary: The text to append

Name: suffix-new-line
Summary: Returns the argument value followed by a space character. If the argument is `null`, it returns `null`.

Name: suffix-space
Summary: Returns the argument value followed by a space character. If the argument is `null`, it returns `null`.

Name: swap-case
Summary: Returns the input text with lowercase characters converted to uppercase and uppercase characters converted to lowercase. Returns `null` when the input is `null`, `DBNull`, `(null)`, or a zero-length array.

Name: text-to-html
Summary: Returns the argument value converted to an HTML-encoded string

Name: text-to-mask
Summary: Returns the argument value formatted according to the mask specified as parameter. Each asterisk (`*`) of the mask is replaced by the corresponding character in the argument value. Other charachters of the mask are not substitued. If the length of the argument value is less than the count of charachetsr that must be replaced in the mask, the last asterisk characters are not replaced.

Parameters.Name: mask
Parameters.Summary: The string representing the mask to apply to the argument string.

Name: title-case
Summary: Returns the input text in title case, capitalizing words while keeping small words lowercase only when they are neither first nor last and do not follow a colon. The first and last words are always capitalized, and a small word after a colon is capitalized. Words containing dots, ampersands, or uppercase letters beyond the first character are treated as already correctly cased and preserved as-is (for example `example.com`, `Q&A`, and `iTunes`). Returns `null` when the input is `null`, `DBNull`, `(null)`, or a zero-length array.

Name: token
Summary: Returns the token at the specified index in the argument value. The index of the first token is 0, the second token is 1, and so on. By default, the tokenization is executed based on any white-space characters. If a character is specified then the tokenization is executed based on this character to separate two tokens.

Parameters.Name: index
Parameters.Summary: An integer value between 0 and +Infinity, defining the position of the token to be returned.

Parameters.Name: separator
Parameters.Summary: A character that delimits the substrings in this instance.

Name: token-count
Summary: Returns the count of token within the argument value. By default, the tokenization is executed based on any white-space characters. If a character is specified then the tokenization is executed based on this character to separate two tokens.

Parameters.Name: separator
Parameters.Summary: A character that delimits the substrings in this instance.

Name: train-case
Summary: Returns the input text in Train-Case, capitalizing each word and joining them with hyphens. Returns empty text when the input is `null`, `empty`, `blank`, or a zero-length array.

Name: upper
Summary: Returns the input text converted to uppercase using invariant culture rules. Returns `null` when the input is `null`, `DBNull`, `(null)`, or a zero-length array.

Name: text-to-datetime
Summary: Returns a dateTime value matching the argument value parsed by the long format in the culture specified in parameter.

Parameters.Name: format
Parameters.Summary: A string representing the required format.

Parameters.Name: culture
Parameters.Summary: A string representing a pre-defined culture.

Name: clean-whitespace
Summary: returns the argument with any whitespace replaced by a space character. `\r\n` is considered as a single character.

Name: collapse-whitespace
Summary: returns the argument with any two or more consecutive whitespaces replaced by the first whitespace in the sequence and trimming the result. `\r\n` is considered as a single character.

Name: trim
Summary: Returns the argument value without all leading or trailing white-space characters.

Name: whitespaces-to-empty
Summary: Returns the argument value except if this value only contains white-space characters then it returns `empty`.

Name: whitespaces-to-null
Summary: Returns the argument value except if this value only contains white-space characters then it returns `null`.

Name: without-diacritics
Summary: Returns the argument string without diacritics.

Name: without-whitespaces
Summary: Returns the argument string without white-space characters.

Name: slug
Summary: Returns a lowercase, separator-normalized slug, removing Latin diacritics without transliterating non-Latin scripts. Returns empty text when the input is `null`, empty, or blank.
